Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah﴾, i.e., in the Hereafter, and does righteous deeds seeking what is with Allah of abundant reward, then indeed Allah will fulfill his hope for him and will repay him his deeds in full and abundantly [[In A: "mawfuran".]], for that is certainly going to happen, because He is All-Hearing of supplication and All-Seeing of all beings [[In T: "basir bil-kainat".]]. Therefore He said: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, then indeed the term of Allah is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever strives, he strives only for himself﴾, like His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self﴾ [Fussilat: 46], i.e., whoever does righteous deeds, the benefit of his deed returns only to himself, for Allah is free of need from the actions of the servants. Even if all of them were upon the most pious heart of one man [among them], that would not increase His dominion by anything. Therefore He said: ﴿And whoever strives, he strives only for himself. Indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Indeed a man strives, while he has never once struck with a sword in all his life."

Then He informed that, although He is free of need from all creation, out of His kindness and beneficence toward them He recompenses those who believe and do righteous deeds with the best of recompense, which is that He removes from them the worst of what they did and rewards them their reward according to the best of what they used to do. He accepts the little of good deeds and rewards for each one ten times its like up to seven hundred fold, and He repays an evil deed with its like or pardons and overlooks, as the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong an atom's weight; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward﴾ [An-Nisa: 40]. And here He said: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely remove from them their evil deeds and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾.

He, the Exalted, says, commanding His servants to show kindness to their parents after exhorting them to hold fast to His oneness (tawhid). Parents are the cause of a person's existence, and they are owed the utmost kindness. The father provides through spending, and the mother through compassion.

For this reason, He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be kind to parents. Whether one or both of them reach old age with you, do not say to them "uff" and do not repel them, but speak to them a generous word. And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, and say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they raised me when I was small."﴾ [al-Isra: 23-24]

Along with this charge to gentleness, mercy and kindness towards them, in return for their earlier kindness, He said: ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them.﴾ That is: even if they are intent on making you follow their religion while they are polytheists, beware of them and obey them not in that. For your return is to Me on the Day of Resurrection, and I will reward you for your kindness to them and your patience in your religion, and I will resurrect you with the righteous, not in the company of your parents, even if you were the closest of people to them in this world. For a person will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection with whom he loved, that is, love based on religion. For this reason He said: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will surely admit them among the righteous.﴾

Al-Tirmidhi, in his commentary on this verse, narrated: Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Simak ibn Harb, who said: I heard Mus'ab ibn Sa'd narrate from his father Sa'd, who said: Four verses were revealed concerning me. Then he mentioned a story, and Umm Sa'd said: "Has not Allah commanded you to honour your parents? By Allah, I will not eat food or drink water until I die or you disbelieve." He said: So whenever they wanted to feed her, they would force open her mouth. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents, but if they strive with you...﴾ the verse.

This hadith was narrated by Imam Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, and also al-Nasa'i. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3079), al-Musnad (1/181), Sahih Muslim no. (1748), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2740).] Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih (good and authentic).

Allah says, informing about the characteristics of a group of the deniers [of the truth] [[addition from F, A.]] who claim faith with their tongues while faith has not taken root in their hearts: that when a trial and a tribulation come upon them in this world, they believe that this is a punishment from Allah upon them, so they apostatize from Islam. For this reason He says: ﴿And among the people is one who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he regards the trial of people as the punishment of Allah.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: "It means that his trial is that he turns away from his religion when he is harmed for the sake of Allah." Likewise said others among the scholars of the early generations (al-salaf). This verse is like His saying: ﴿And among the people is one who worships Allah on an edge; if good befalls him, he is content with it, but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face. He has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss.﴾ [al-Hajj: 11].

Then He says: ﴿And if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you."﴾ That is: and if a near victory comes from your Lord, O Muhammad, and conquest and spoils, these people will surely say to you, "Indeed, we were with you," meaning [we were] [[addition from F.]] your brothers in religion. As He, Exalted, said: ﴿Those who wait and watch you: if there is a victory for you from Allah, they say, "Were we not with you?" And if the disbelievers have a share, they say, "Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?"﴾ [an-Nisa': 141]. And He said: ﴿So perhaps Allah will bring a conquest or a command from Him, and they will become regretful for what they had concealed within themselves.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 52].

And He, Exalted, said, informing about them here: ﴿And if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you."﴾ Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the breasts of the worlds?﴾ That is: Is not Allah most knowing of what is in their hearts and what their inner selves conceal, even if they show you agreement?

As He, Exalted, said: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those among you who strive and who are patient, and We will test your reports.﴾ [Muhammad: 31]. This is a consolation from Allah to His servant and messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), informing him about Noah (peace be upon him): that he remained among his people this long period calling them to Allah night and day, secretly and openly, yet this only increased them in flight from the truth, turning away from it and denying him, and only a few of them believed with him. Therefore He said: ﴿So he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years, then the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers﴾. That is: after this long period, the conveying and warning had no effect on them. So you, O Muhammad, do not grieve over those of your people who disbelieved in you, and do not be saddened about them, for Allah guides whom He wills and leads astray whom He wills, the command is in His hand, and to Him all matters are returned. ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe. Even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 96-97]. And know that Allah will surely make you prevail, support you, strengthen you, humiliate your enemy, subdue them, and make them the lowest of the low.

Hammad ibn Salamah said, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mahak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Noah was sent when he was forty years old, and he remained among his people a thousand years less fifty years, and lived after the flood sixty years, until the people multiplied and spread.

Qatadah said: It is said that his whole lifespan was a thousand years less fifty years; he remained among them three hundred years before calling them, and called them three hundred years, and remained after the flood three hundred and fifty years.

This is a strange statement. The apparent context of the verse is that he remained among his people calling them to Allah for a thousand years less fifty years.

Awn ibn Abi Shaddad said: Allah sent Noah to his people when he was three hundred and fifty years old, so he called them for a thousand years less fifty years, then he lived after that three hundred and fifty years.

This too is strange. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it, and the statement of Ibn Abbas is closer to correct, and Allah knows best.

Al-Thawri said, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Mujahid, who said: Ibn Umar said to me, "How long did Noah remain among his people?" I said, "A thousand years less fifty years." He said: "The people have not ceased to decline in their lifespans, their intellects and their characters until this day of yours."

His saying: ﴿So We saved him and the companions of the ship﴾ means: those who believed in Noah (peace be upon him). This has been mentioned in detail in Surah Hud, and its explanation was given there sufficiently so that it need not be repeated.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We made it a sign for the worlds﴾ means: We made that ship remain, either the ship itself, as Qatadah said: it remained until the beginning of Islam upon the mountain of al-Judi; or its kind, which He made as a reminder to people of His blessings upon creation, how He saved them from the flood. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship. And We created for them of its likeness that they ride. And if We willed, We would drown them, and there would be no one to answer their cry, nor would they be saved, except by mercy from Us and as enjoyment for a time﴾ [Ya-Sin: 41-44]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, when the water rose high, We carried you in the sailing ship, that We might make it for you a reminder and that an attentive ear would retain it﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 11-12]. And here He said: ﴿So We saved him and the companions of the ship and made it a sign for the worlds﴾. This is from the method of moving from the specific individual to the general category, like His saying: ﴿And We have certainly adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and made them missiles against the devils﴾ [Al-Mulk: 5], meaning: We made their kind. For those by which devils are pelted are not the same as the adornment of the sky. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did certainly create man from an extract of clay. Then We made him a drop [of sperm] in a firm place﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 12-13]. There are many similar examples of this.

Ibn Jarir said: If it were said that the pronoun in His saying ﴿and made it﴾ refers to the punishment, it would be a valid view, and Allah knows best.

The Most High informs us about His servant, messenger and intimate friend Ibrahim (Abraham), the leader of the ḥunafā' (those who turn sincerely to God): that he called his people to worship God alone, without partner, and to devote themselves sincerely to Him in piety, to seek provision from Him alone without partner, and to affirm His unity in gratitude (*al-shukr*), since He is the one who is thanked for blessings and no one else grants them. So he said to his people: ﴿Worship God and fear Him﴾, meaning: devote worship and fear to Him sincerely. ﴿That is better for you, if you only knew﴾, meaning: if you do this, good will come to you in this world and the next, and evil will be averted from you in this world and the next.

Then he informed them that the idols they worship and the images are neither harmful nor beneficial, and that it is you who invented names for them, calling them gods, when they are only creatures like you. This is how al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and Mujahid and al-Suddi said the same.

Al-Walibi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿and you fabricate a falsehood﴾, meaning: you carve them into idols. Mujahid, in one narration, said the same, as did 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah and others, and Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may God have mercy on him, preferred this view.

﴿They possess no provision for you; so seek provision from God﴾. This expression is more emphatic in restricting (the provision to God), like His saying: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ (Al-Fatihah: 5), and ﴿My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise﴾ (Al-Tahrim: 11). Therefore He said: ﴿so seek﴾, meaning: ask, ﴿provision from God﴾, meaning: not from other than Him, for other than Him possesses nothing. ﴿Worship Him and be grateful to Him﴾, meaning: eat of His provision, worship Him alone, and give thanks to Him for what He has bestowed upon you. ﴿To Him you will be returned﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection, when He will recompense every doer for his deeds.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if you deny, then communities before you have denied﴾, meaning: and the news has reached you of what befell them of punishment and chastisement for opposing the messengers. ﴿And the messenger is only responsible for clear communication﴾, meaning: the messenger's duty is only to convey to you what God the Most High has commanded him of the message, while God leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So strive for your own sake to be among the fortunate.

Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And if you deny, then communities before you have denied﴾, said: this consoles His Prophet (ﷺ). This view of Qatadah implies that the first speech had ended and that this is an interjection leading up to His saying ﴿So what was the answer of his people﴾. Ibn Jarir also explicitly stated this.

The apparent context indicates that all of this is the speech of Ibrahim the intimate friend, peace be upon him, [to his people], arguing with them to establish the return (to God), as shown by his saying after all of this: ﴿So what was the answer of his people﴾. And God knows best.

Allah says, relating about the Friend (Khalil, Ibrahim) peace be upon him, that he guided them to affirm the Return (al-Ma'ad) which they denied, through what they witness in themselves of Allah's creating them after they were not a thing mentioned. Then they came into being and became people who hear and see. So He who originated this is able to restore it, for it is easy for Him and effortless before Him.

Then he guided them to take heed of the signs visible in the horizons of Allah's creation of things: the heavens and what is in them of shining stars, the fixed ones and the wandering ones (planets), and the earths and what is in them of expanses, mountains, valleys, deserts, wastelands, trees, rivers, fruits and seas. Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 29, verses 24–25:

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about the people of Abraham (ﷺ) in their disbelief, their obstinacy, their arrogance, and their rejection of the truth with falsehood: Indeed, they had no answer after this statement of Abraham's, which contained guidance and clarification, ﴿except that they said, "Kill him or burn him."﴾ That was because the proof had been established against them and the argument had been directed at them, so they turned to using their status and the strength of their kingdom. ﴿They said, "Build for him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire." So they intended a scheme against him, but We made them the lowest.﴾ [al-Saffat: 97–98]. That is because they gathered great quantities of firewood over a long period, enclosed it, and then set fire to it, so that its flames rose up to the clouds of the sky. No fire was ever kindled greater than it. Then they targeted Abraham, bound him, and placed him in the pan of the catapult (manjaniq), then hurled him into it. But Allah made it cool and safe for him, and he came out of it unharmed after remaining in it for some days. For this and similar acts, Allah made him a leader for mankind. He gave his self to the Merciful, his body to the fires, offered his son in sacrifice, and made his wealth available to guests. For this reason, all the people of the religions have agreed on love for him.

* *

His statement, ﴿So Allah rescued him from the fire﴾, means: Allah delivered him from it by making it cool and safe for him. ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ ﴿And he said, "You have taken only idols instead of Allah out of affection among yourselves in the life of this world."﴾ He says to his people, rebuking them and censuring them for the evil of their conduct in worshipping idols: You have taken these only so that you would gather in worshipping them in this world, out of friendship and mutual attachment among yourselves, each one toward the other, in the life of this world. This is according to the reading of the one who put ﴿مَوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكُمْ﴾ (mawaddata baynikum, "affection among yourselves") in the accusative, as an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu). As for the reading in the nominative, its meaning is: Your taking this (idol-worship) only produces affection for you in this world alone. ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection﴾ this situation will be reversed, and this friendship and affection will remain as hatred and enmity. ﴿Some of you will disavow others﴾, meaning you will deny what was between you. ﴿And some of you will curse others﴾, meaning the followers will curse the leaders, and the leaders will curse the followers. ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾ [al-A'raf: 38]. Allah, exalted is He, also said: ﴿Close friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67]. And here He said: ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disavow others and some of you will curse others, and your refuge is the Fire, and you will have no helpers.﴾ That is, your destination and return after the plains of the Resurrection will be the Fire, and you will have no helper to aid you or rescuer to save you from the punishment of Allah. This is the condition of the disbelievers; as for the believers, it is the opposite of that.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi related to us: Abu 'Asim al-Thaqafi related to us: al-Rabi' ibn Isma'il ibn 'Amr ibn Sa'id ibn Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah al-Makhzumi related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from Umm Hani' (sister of Ali ibn Abi Talib), who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "I will inform you that Allah, the Exalted, will gather the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection in one level plain. So who knows where the two parties will be?" She said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." Then he said: "Then a caller will call from beneath the Throne: 'O people of monotheism!' So they will raise their heads," (Abu 'Asim said: they will raise their heads). "Then he will call: 'O people of monotheism!' Then he will call a third time: 'O people of monotheism, indeed Allah has pardoned you.'" He said: "The people will say: 'Some of them have clung to others because of the oppressions of the world,' meaning the injustices. Then He will call: 'O people of monotheism, let some of you pardon others, and the reward is with Allah.'"

[Note: Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. 4803, through the route of Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi with this chain, and said: "It is not narrated from Umm Hani' except with this chain; Abu 'Asim alone transmitted it." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/355): "In its chain is Abu 'Asim, al-Rabi' ibn Isma'il, who is munkar al-hadith (rejected in narration), as Abu Hatim said."]

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, relating from Ibrahim: "Lut believed in him." It is said that he was the son of Ibrahim's brother; they say he was Lut ibn Haran ibn Azar. This means that no one from his people believed in him apart from Lut, and Sarah was the wife of [Ibrahim] the Friend (al-Khalil). But the question arises: how is this verse reconciled with the hadith reported in Sahih [Muslim, no. 2371], that when Ibrahim passed by that tyrant, he asked Ibrahim about Sarah, "What is she to him?" and he said, "[She is] my sister." Then he came to her and said: "I have told him, 'You are my sister,' so do not contradict me, for there is no believer on the face of the earth except you and me, so you are my sister in religion." It seems that what is meant by this, and Allah knows best, is that there were no two spouses upon Islam on the face of the earth except me and you. As for Lut, peace be upon him, he believed in him from among his people, emigrated with him to the land of Sham, and then was sent during the lifetime of the Friend to the people of "Sodom" (Sadum) and its region, and what happened to them has been mentioned before and will come later.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord."﴾ The pronoun in His saying ﴿And he said﴾ may refer to Lut, since he is the nearer of the two mentioned, and it may refer to Ibrahim. This is the view of Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak, and the one referred to by His saying ﴿So Lut believed in him﴾, i.e., from among his people.

Then Allah informed about him that he chose to emigrate from among his people, seeking to manifest the religion and to be able to do so. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, He is the Almighty﴾, i.e., to Him belongs might, and to His Messenger and to the believers in Him, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His sayings, His actions, and His decrees, both the divine decrees and the legislative rulings.

Qatadah said: "Both of them emigrated from Kuthaa, which is from the outskirts of Kufa, to Sham." He said: "It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: 'There will be a migration after a migration; the people of the earth will gather to the place of migration of Ibrahim, and the worst of its people will remain in the earth, until their land vomits them out and the Spirit of Allah loathes them, and the Fire will gather them together with the monkeys and the swine; it will spend the night with them when they spend the night, and take its noon rest with them when they rest, and it will eat what falls from them.'"

Imam Ahmad has traced this hadith with a chain, narrating it in full from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: "Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: When the pledge of allegiance to Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah came to us, I went to Sham and was informed of a place where Nawf al-Bikali would stand, so I went to him. Then a man came, and the people withdrew from him, and he was wearing a striped cloak; and behold, it was Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As. When Nawf saw him, he stopped speaking, and Abdullah said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "There will be a migration after a migration, so the people will gather to the place of migration of Ibrahim, and only the worst of its people will remain; their land will vomit them out, the self of the Most Merciful will loathe them, and the Fire will gather them with the monkeys and the swine; it will spend the night with them when they spend the night, and take its noon rest with them when they rest, and it will eat whoever lags behind from them."' He said: 'And I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "People will come out of my Ummah from the direction of the east, reciting the Qur'an, but it will not pass their collarbones. Every time a generation of them comes out, it will be cut off; every time a generation of them comes out, it will be cut off," until he counted it more than twenty times, "every time a generation of them comes out it will be cut off, until the Dajjal comes out among their remnant."'" Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 29, verse 31–35:

When Lut (peace be upon him) sought help from Allah against them, Allah sent angels to support him. They passed by Ibrahim (peace be upon him) in the form of guests, and he brought them what is fitting for a guest. When he saw that they had no inclination toward the food, he disliked them and felt a fear of them. They began to put him at ease and gave him the good news of a righteous son from his wife Sarah, who was present, and she marvelled at this, as has already been explained in Surah Hud and Surah al-Hijr. When they brought Ibrahim the good news and informed him that they had been sent to destroy the people of Lut, he began to plead on their behalf, hoping they might be given respite, in case Allah would guide them. Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says:

Allah, Exalted is He, informs us about these nations that denied the messengers, how He destroyed them and varied their punishment. So He seized them in retribution against them: 'Ad, the people of Hud, who lived in al-Ahqaf, which is near Hadramawt in the land of Yemen; and Thamud, the people of Salih, who lived in al-Hijr near Wadi al-Qura. The Arabs knew their dwellings well and passed by them often. And Qarun, the owner of great wealth and of the heavy treasure keys; and Pharaoh, king of Egypt in the time of Musa, and his minister Haman, both Copts, disbelievers in Allah and His messenger.

﴿So each We seized for his sin﴾, i.e., his punishment was suited to him. ﴿Among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones﴾, and they were 'Ad. That was because they said: "Who is stronger than us in power?" So there came upon them a violent, cold wind, extremely cold, fierce and very strong in its blowing, which carried against them the pebbles of the earth and overturned them upon them, uprooting them from the earth, lifting the man among them up to the heights of the sky, then turning him upside down onto the top of his head so that it was crushed, leaving a body without a head, as if they were the trunks of uprooted palm trees. ﴿And among them were those seized by the Blast﴾, and they were Thamud. The proof was established against them and the evidence became manifest to them, through that she-camel which emerged from the rock, exactly as they had asked. Yet despite this they did not believe, but persisted in their transgression and disbelief. They threatened the prophet of Allah Salih and those who believed with him, and threatened them that they would expel them and stone them. So there came upon them a Blast that silenced their voices and their movements. ﴿And among them were those We caused the earth to swallow﴾, and he was Qarun, who transgressed, oppressed, and exceeded all bounds, disobeyed the Lord Most High, walked in the earth exultantly, rejoiced, behaved insolently, was deluded by himself, believed himself superior to others, and strutted in his gait. So Allah caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling, and he continues to sink into it until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And among them were those We drowned﴾, and they were Pharaoh and his minister Haman, and his soldiers, all of them, who were drowned in a single morning, so that none of them was left to give news. ﴿And Allah was not one to wrong them﴾, i.e., in what He did to them, ﴿but they were wronging themselves﴾, i.e., He only did that to them as a fitting recompense for what their hands had earned.

What we have mentioned is the apparent context of the verse, and it is of the type of *laff wa nashr* (the arrangement in which items are mentioned and then matched back in order), in that He mentioned the disbelieving nations, then said: ﴿So each We seized for his sin﴾ [the verse], meaning from among those mentioned. This narration from Ibn 'Abbas is disconnected (munqati'), since Ibn Jurayj did not meet him. Moreover, the destruction of the people of Nuh by the flood and of the people of Lut by sending down a punishment from the sky has already been mentioned in this surah, and the context has been long, with a separation between that and this passage.

Qatadah said: ﴿Among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones﴾, he said: the people of Lut; ﴿And among them were those seized by the Blast﴾: the people of Shu'ayb. This is also far-fetched for the reasons already given, and Allah knows best.

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn 'Umar narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic to the people of Islam. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not believe the People of the Book nor disbelieve them, but say: We believe in Allah and what has been sent down to us and what has been sent down to you, and our God and your God is One, and to Him we submit." This hadith is related by al-Bukhari alone [[Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (4485, 7362).]].

Imam Ahmad said: 'Uthman ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, Ibn Abi Namlah informed me that Abu Namlah al-Ansari informed him that while he was sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a man from the Jews came to him and said: "O Muhammad, does this funeral speak?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah knows best." The Jew said: "I testify that it speaks." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the People of the Book tell you something, do not believe them nor disbelieve them, but say: We believe in Allah, His messengers and His books. If it is true, you have not denied them; and if it is false, you have not believed them" [[Al-Musnad (4/136).]].

I say: this Abu Namlah is 'Umarah. It is also said: 'Ammar. It is also said: 'Amr ibn Mu'adh ibn Zurarah al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him.

Then know that most of what they narrate is, for the most part, falsehood and fabrication, because it has been subjected to distortion, alteration, change and misinterpretation. How little of it is truthful! And then how little benefit there is in much of it even if it were authentic.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abu 'Asim narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn 'Amir, from 'Umarah ibn 'Umayr, from Hurayth ibn Zuhayr, from 'Abd Allah — that is Ibn Mas'ud — who said: "Do not ask the People of the Book about anything, for they will never guide you, and they have gone astray. Either you will deny a truth or affirm a falsehood. No one among the People of the Book is without a doubt in his heart that calls him to his religion, like the call of the camel to water" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (21/4).]].

Al-Bukhari said: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, Ibn Shihab informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "How do you ask the People of the Book about anything, when your Book which was sent down to His Messenger (ﷺ) is the most recent, read by you unmixed and unaltered? He has told you that the People of the Book changed the Book of Allah and altered it, and wrote the book with their own hands, and said: 'This is from Allah,' to exchange it for a small price. Does not the knowledge that has come to you prevent you from asking them? No, by Allah, we have never seen any man of them ask you about what was sent down to you" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7363).]].

Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Yaman said: Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me that he heard Mu'awiyah narrating to a group of Quraysh in Madinah — and he mentioned Ka'b al-Ahbar — and said: "If he is among the most truthful of these narrators who relate from the People of the Book, yet even so we test him with lying" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7361).]].

I say: its meaning is that lying occurs from him linguistically without intent, because he narrates from scriptures in which he has good faith, while among them are things that are fabricated and false; for there were not among their community memorizers and precise transmitters like this great Ummah. Yet despite that, and the nearness of the era, many hadiths were fabricated in this Ummah, which none knows except Allah and whomever Allah grants knowledge of that, each according to his measure. And to Allah belong praise and grace.

Ibn Jarir said: Allah Most High says: Just as We sent down the Scriptures (al-Kutub) to those prophets who came before you, O Muhammad, so have We sent down to you this Book.

This which he has said is good, and its connection and linkage (munasabah wa irtibat) is excellent.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recite it﴾, meaning: those who received it and recited it as it ought to be recited, from among their learned rabbis who were intelligent, such as Abdullah ibn Salam, Salman al-Farisi, and their like.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And among these there are those who believe in it﴾, meaning the Arabs of Quraysh and others, ﴿and none deny Our signs except the disbelievers﴾, that is: none reject them and deny their truth except those who conceal the truth with falsehood and cover the light of the sun with the (dark) shades of falsehood, and far-fetched is that.

Then Allah Most High said: ﴿And you did not recite before it any Book, nor did you write it with your right hand﴾, that is: O Muhammad, you lived among your people for a lifetime before you brought this Qur'an, without reading any book and without being skilled at writing. Rather, everyone among your people and others knows that you are an unlettered man who neither reads nor writes. Such is also his description in the earlier Scriptures, as Allah Most High said: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong﴾ [al-A'raf: 157]. And so he remained, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, forever until the Day of Resurrection: he did not write well, nor did he write a line or a letter with his own hand. Rather, he had scribes who wrote the revelation and the letters to the regions before him. As for some later jurists, such as the judge Abu al-Walid al-Baji and those who followed him, who claimed that he, peace be upon him, wrote on the day of Hudaybiyyah: "This is what Muhammad ibn Abdullah has agreed upon," what led him to this was a report in Sahih al-Bukhari: "Then he took and wrote," and this is to be understood in light of the other report: "Then he commanded and it was written." For this reason, the jurists of the West and the East vehemently rejected whoever said what al-Baji said, disassociated themselves from him, recited verses about it, and delivered sermons on it in their gatherings. What the man intended (I mean al-Baji, as appears from him) was that he wrote that as a miracle, not that he was skilled at writing, just as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said in describing the Dajjal: "Written between his eyes is 'Kafir,'" and in another narration: "K-F-R, which every believer will read." (Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 7131, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him.) As for what some have cited, that he did not die until he learned writing, it is weak and has no basis. Allah Most High said: ﴿And you did not recite﴾, that is, read, ﴿before it any Book﴾, to emphasize the negation, ﴿nor did you write it with your right hand﴾, which is also for emphasis, and it came in the manner of what is usual, as in His saying: ﴿nor a bird that flies with its two wings﴾ [al-An'am: 38].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Otherwise the falsifiers would have had cause for doubt﴾, that is: if you had been skilled at writing, some ignorant people would have doubted and said: "He learned this from earlier books transmitted from the prophets," even though they said this while knowing that he was unlettered and did not write well: ﴿And they say: "Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, and which are dictated to him morning and evening"﴾ [al-Furqan: 5]. Allah Most High said: ﴿Say: "It was sent down by the One who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth; indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful"﴾ [al-Furqan: 6]. And here He said: ﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾, that is: this Qur'an is clear signs, manifest in indicating the truth, in command, prohibition and information, which the scholars memorize. Allah has made it easy for them to memorize, recite and interpret it, as Allah Most High said: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [al-Qamar: 17]. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No prophet has been given except what people believed in because of its like, but what I was given is a revelation which Allah revealed to me, so I hope to be the one with the most followers."(Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 7274, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, and it will come, Allah willing.)

In the hadith of Iyad ibn Himar, in Sahih Muslim: "Allah Most High says: 'Indeed I will test you and test through you, and I will send down to you a Book which water cannot wash away; you will recite it asleep and awake.'" (Sahih Muslim, no. 2865.) That is: if water were to wash the place where it is written, one would not need that place, as came in another hadith: "If the Qur'an were in a hide, fire would not burn it." (Reported by Ahmad in his Musnad (4/151) from Uqbah ibn Amir; its discussion has preceded in the chapter on the virtues of the Qur'an.) Because it is preserved in the breasts, made easy on the tongues, and guarded in the hearts, and it is inimitable in wording and meaning. For this reason it is mentioned in earlier Scriptures, describing this Ummah: "Their Gospels are in their breasts."

Ibn Jarir chose that the meaning of His saying: ﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾ is: rather, the knowledge that you did not recite any book before this one nor write it with your right hand is clear signs in the breasts of those given knowledge among the People of the Book. He transmitted this from Qatadah and Ibn Jurayj, and he related the first view only from al-Hasan al-Basri.

I say: This is what al-Awfi related from Abdullah ibn Abbas, and what al-Dahhak said, and it is the more apparent, and Allah knows best.

Then the Almighty said, showing the extent of their ignorance and the feebleness of their intellects, in that they asked for signs that would show them the truthfulness of Muhammad in what he brought them, while He had already brought them the Mighty Book, ﴿to which falsehood cannot come from before it or behind it, a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy﴾, which is greater than every miracle, since the eloquent and the masters of rhetoric were unable to oppose it, not even to oppose ten surahs like it, nor even a single surah of it. So He said: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, which is recited to them?﴾ That is, is it not enough for them as a sign that We have sent down to you this great Book, in which there is the news of those before them, the report of those after them, and the judgment among them? As He says: ﴿Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 197] And He says: ﴿They say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?" Has there not come to them the clear evidence of what is in the earlier scriptures?﴾ [Ta-Ha: 133]

Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id narrated to me, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There was no prophet among the prophets except that he was given signs of the kind that people believed in because of them. This is a command from Allah to His believing servants to emigrate from a land where they cannot establish the religion, to the wide earth of Allah, where establishing the religion is possible, so that they may affirm Allah's oneness and worship Him as He has commanded them. Therefore He said: ﴿O My servants who believe, indeed My earth is vast, so worship Me alone.﴾

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Abd Rabbih narrated to us, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Jubayr ibn Amr al-Qurashi narrated to me, Abu Sa'd al-Ansari narrated to me, from Abu Yahya, the freed slave (mawla) of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The lands are Allah's lands, and the servants are Allah's servants; wherever you find good, then settle there."¹

Thus, when the weak among the Muslims in Makkah found it too constricted to remain there, they went out as emigrants to the land of Abyssinia (al-Habasha), so that they could be safe in their religion there. There they found the best of the two abodes: the Negus (al-Najashi), the king of Abyssinia, Ashama, may Allah have mercy on him, who gave them refuge, supported them with his help, and made them secure in his land. Afterwards, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his remaining companions emigrated to the blessed city of Yathrib, Madinah the radiant.²

Then He said: ﴿Every soul shall taste death; then to Us you will be returned.﴾ That is: wherever you are, death will overtake you, so be in obedience to Allah and where Allah has commanded you, for that is better for you, since death is unavoidable and there is no escape from it. Then the return (al-marji' wa'l-ma'ab) is to Allah. Whoever is obedient to Him, He will reward with the best reward and grant him complete recompense. Therefore He said: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds—We will surely settle them in lofty chambers in Paradise, beneath which rivers flow,﴾ that is: We will surely house them in elevated dwellings in Paradise, beneath which rivers flow, of various kinds: of water, wine, honey and milk, which they will direct and channel wherever they wish; ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, that is: remaining in them eternally, never desiring to be moved from them; ﴿how excellent is the reward of the workers﴾: how excellent these chambers are as a reward for the deeds of the believers.

﴿Those who are patient﴾, that is: patient in their religion, who emigrated to Allah, opposed the enemies, separated from family and relatives, seeking the face of Allah, hoping for what is with Him, and trusting in the truth of His promise.

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: My father narrated to me, Safwan al-Mu'adhdhin narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Sallam narrated to us, from his brother Zayd ibn Sallam, from his grandfather Abu Sallam al-Aswad, who said: Abu Ma'atiq al-Ash'ari narrated to me that Abu Malik al-Ash'ari told him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told him: "Indeed in Paradise there are chambers whose exterior can be seen from the interior and whose interior can be seen from the exterior, which Allah has prepared for those who feed the food, speak good words, fast regularly, and establish prayer while people are asleep."³

And His saying: ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾, in all their circumstances, in their religion and their worldly affairs.

Then Allah informed them that provision is not restricted to one place; rather His provision is general for His creation wherever they are and wherever they may be. Indeed, the provisions of the emigrants, wherever they emigrated, became greater, wider and better, for after a little while they became the rulers of the lands in all regions and cities. Therefore He said: ﴿And how many a creature there is that does not carry its provision﴾, that is: it cannot gather and acquire it, and does not store anything for tomorrow; ﴿Allah provides for it and for you﴾, that is: Allah arranges its provision despite its weakness and makes it easy for it, sending to every creature the provision that suits it, even the ant in the depths of the earth, the bird in the air, and the fish in the water. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon Allah; and He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage. All is in a clear register.﴾ [Hud: 6]

She said: The Negus wept until his beard was wet, and his bishops wept until their scriptures were wet, when they heard what was recited to them. The Negus said: Indeed this and what Moses brought have come from the same niche (mishkah). Go, by Allah, I will not hand them over to you, nor will I betray them. She said: When they left his presence, Amr ibn al-'As said: By Allah, I will go to him tomorrow and tell him something by which I will uproot their stronghold (khadra'ahum).

She said: Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'ah—and he was the more God-fearing of the two of us—said to him: Do not do that, for they have ties of kinship with us, even though they have opposed us. He said: By Allah, I will inform him that they say a dreadful thing about Jesus. Then he sent to them to ask them what they say about him. She said: He sent for them to question them about it. She said: Nothing like this had ever befallen us. The people gathered and some said to others: What will you say about Jesus if he asks you about him? They said: We will say what Allah the Mighty and Majestic said and what our Prophet brought, whatever the outcome may be. She said: When they entered upon him, he said to them: What do you say about Jesus son of Mary? She said: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib said: We say about him what our Prophet (ﷺ) brought: he is the servant of Allah, His Messenger, His spirit, and His word which He cast to Mary the virgin, the pure. She said: The Negus struck the ground with his hand, took a stick from it, and said to him: Jesus son of Mary exceeds what you said by no more than this stick.

She said: His patriarchs snorted around him when he said what he said. He said: Even if you snort, go, for you are secure (shiyum) in my land. The shiyum are the secure. By Allah, Allah did not take bribery from me when He restored my kingship to me, so that I should take bribes concerning it, nor did He obey people concerning me, so that I should obey them concerning Him. As for the words of the Exalted: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, meaning: He hears the words of His servants and knows their movements and their stillness.

This is a command from Allah to His believing servants to emigrate from a land where they cannot establish the religion, to the wide earth of Allah, where establishing the religion is possible, so that they may affirm Allah's oneness and worship Him as He has commanded them. Therefore He said: ﴿O My servants who believe, indeed My earth is vast, so worship Me alone.﴾

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Abd Rabbih narrated to us, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Jubayr ibn Amr al-Qurashi narrated to me, Abu Sa'd al-Ansari narrated to me, from Abu Yahya, the freed slave (mawla) of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The lands are Allah's lands, and the servants are Allah's servants; wherever you find good, then settle there."¹

Thus, when the weak among the Muslims in Makkah found it too constricted to remain there, they went out as emigrants to the land of Abyssinia (al-Habasha), so that they could be safe in their religion there. There they found the best of the two abodes: the Negus (al-Najashi), the king of Abyssinia, Ashama, may Allah have mercy on him, who gave them refuge, supported them with his help, and made them secure in his land. Afterwards, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his remaining companions emigrated to the blessed city of Yathrib, Madinah the radiant.²

Then He said: ﴿Every soul shall taste death; then to Us you will be returned.﴾ That is: wherever you are, death will overtake you, so be in obedience to Allah and where Allah has commanded you, for that is better for you, since death is unavoidable and there is no escape from it. Then the return (al-marji' wa'l-ma'ab) is to Allah. Whoever is obedient to Him, He will reward with the best reward and grant him complete recompense. Therefore He said: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds—We will surely settle them in lofty chambers in Paradise, beneath which rivers flow,﴾ that is: We will surely house them in elevated dwellings in Paradise, beneath which rivers flow, of various kinds: of water, wine, honey and milk, which they will direct and channel wherever they wish; ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, that is: remaining in them eternally, never desiring to be moved from them; ﴿how excellent is the reward of the workers﴾: how excellent these chambers are as a reward for the deeds of the believers.

﴿Those who are patient﴾, that is: patient in their religion, who emigrated to Allah, opposed the enemies, separated from family and relatives, seeking the face of Allah, hoping for what is with Him, and trusting in the truth of His promise.

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: My father narrated to me, Safwan al-Mu'adhdhin narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Sallam narrated to us, from his brother Zayd ibn Sallam, from his grandfather Abu Sallam al-Aswad, who said: Abu Ma'atiq al-Ash'ari narrated to me that Abu Malik al-Ash'ari told him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told him: "Indeed in Paradise there are chambers whose exterior can be seen from the interior and whose interior can be seen from the exterior, which Allah has prepared for those who feed the food, speak good words, fast regularly, and establish prayer while people are asleep."³

And His saying: ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾, in all their circumstances, in their religion and their worldly affairs.

Then Allah informed them that provision is not restricted to one place; rather His provision is general for His creation wherever they are and wherever they may be. Indeed, the provisions of the emigrants, wherever they emigrated, became greater, wider and better, for after a little while they became the rulers of the lands in all regions and cities. Therefore He said: ﴿And how many a creature there is that does not carry its provision﴾, that is: it cannot gather and acquire it, and does not store anything for tomorrow; ﴿Allah provides for it and for you﴾, that is: Allah arranges its provision despite its weakness and makes it easy for it, sending to every creature the provision that suits it, even the ant in the depths of the earth, the bird in the air, and the fish in the water. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon Allah; and He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage. All is in a clear register.﴾ [Hud: 6]

If they are as these two claim, I will hand them over to them and return them to their country; but if it is otherwise, I will protect them and treat them well as long as they neighbor me and dwell in my land.

She said: Then he sent for the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and summoned them. When his messenger came to them, they gathered, and some of them said to others: What will you say to this man when you come to him? They said: We will say: By Allah, we know only what our Prophet (ﷺ) taught us and commanded us, whatever the outcome may be. She said: When they came to him, the Negus had summoned his bishops, who spread their scriptures around him. When they entered upon him, he asked them: What is this religion for which you have separated from your people, and have not entered my religion or the religion of any of these communities?

She said: The one who spoke to him was Ja'far ibn Abi Talib. He said: O King, we were a people of ignorance, worshipping idols, eating carrion, committing abominations, severing family ties, mistreating neighbors, and the strong among us devouring the weak. We were in that state until Allah sent to us a Messenger whose lineage, truthfulness, trustworthiness and chastity we knew. He called us to Allah, to affirm His oneness, and to renounce what we and our fathers used to worship besides Him—stones and idols. He commanded us to speak the truth, to fulfill trusts, to maintain family ties, to be good to neighbors, and to refrain from what is forbidden and from bloodshed. He forbade us from abominations, false speech, devouring the property of orphans, and slandering chaste women. He commanded us to worship Allah alone and not associate anything with Him, and commanded us to pray, to give zakat and to fast. She said: He then enumerated for him the matters of Islam. We believed him, affirmed him, and followed him in what he brought from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So we worshipped Allah, associating nothing with Him, made unlawful what He made unlawful for us, and made lawful what He made lawful. Then our people attacked us, tortured us, and tempted us away from our religion, to return us from worshipping Allah to worshipping idols, and to make lawful for us the impure things as they had been lawful for them. When they overpowered us, oppressed us, constricted us, and stood between us and our religion, we went out to your land, chose you over others, desired your protection, and hoped that we would not be wronged in your presence, O King.

She said: The Negus said to him: Do you have anything of what he brought from Allah? She said: Ja'far said: Yes. The Negus said: Then recite it to me. So he recited to him the beginning of (Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad) [Maryam].

She said: The Negus wept until his beard was wet, and his bishops wept until their scriptures were wet, when they heard what was recited to them. The Negus said: Indeed this and what Moses brought have come from the same niche (mishkah). Go, by Allah, I will not hand them over to you, nor will I betray them. She said: When they left his presence, Amr ibn al-'As said: By Allah, I will go to him tomorrow and tell him something by which I will uproot their stronghold (khadra'ahum).

She said: Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'ah—and he was the more God-fearing of the two of us—said to him: Do not do that, for they have ties of kinship with us, even though they have opposed us. She said: When they entered upon him, he said to them: What do you say about Jesus son of Mary? She said: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib said: We say about him what our Prophet (ﷺ) brought: he is the servant of Allah, His Messenger, His spirit, and His word which He cast to Mary the virgin, the pure. She said: The Negus struck the ground with his hand, took a stick from it, and said to him: Jesus son of Mary exceeds what you said by no more than this stick.

She said: His patriarchs snorted around him when he said what he said. He said: Even if you snort, go, for you are secure (shiyum) in my land. The shiyum are the secure. Whoever insults you will pay a fine; whoever insults you will pay a fine. I would not like to have a mountain of gold and to have harmed a man among you. By Allah, Allah did not take bribery from me when He restored my kingship to me, so that I should take bribes concerning it, nor did He obey people concerning me, so that I should obey them concerning Him. She said: By Allah, we had not remained long in that condition when a man from Abyssinia rose up to contest his kingship. She said: By Allah, we had never known a sorrow greater than the sorrow we felt then, fearing that this man would prevail over the Negus, and that there would come a ruler who did not recognize our rights as the Negus had recognized them. She said: The Negus marched against him, with the Nile lying between them. She said: By Allah, while we were in that state, awaiting what would happen, behold, al-Zubayr came running, waving his garment, crying: Rejoice! The Negus has prevailed, and Allah has destroyed his enemy. By Allah, we had never been so joyful as we were then. She said: The Negus returned, Allah destroyed his enemy, established his authority in his land, and the affairs of Abyssinia were settled for him. We remained with him in the best dwelling until we came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was in Makkah.

It is narrated from al-Zubayr who said: When the enemy of the Negus, from among the people of his land, attacked him, the emigrants came to him and said: We wish to go out against them and fight alongside you, and you will see our boldness, and we will reward you for what you have done for us. He said: One whom Allah helps is better than one whom people help. He then rejected that from them.

Then He said: ﴿Every soul shall taste death; then to Us you will be returned.﴾

They have mentioned that when the raven hatches its young from eggs, they come out white. When their parents see them thus, they shun them for days until the feathers turn black. The chick remains with its mouth open, seeking its parents, and Allah makes available for it small insects like gnats, which come to it, and it feeds on them during those days until its feathers blacken. Both parents keep checking on it at all times. Whenever they see it with white feathers, they shun it, but when they see its feathers have turned black, they turn to it with care and provision. For this reason the poet said:

O Provider of the young raven in its nest,
and Mender of the broken, shattered bone...

As for the words of the Exalted: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, meaning: He hears the words of His servants and knows their movements and their stillness.

This is a command from Allah to His believing servants to emigrate from a land where they cannot establish the religion, to the wide earth of Allah, where establishing the religion is possible, so that they may affirm Allah's oneness and worship Him as He has commanded them. Therefore He said: ﴿O My servants who believe, indeed My earth is vast, so worship Me alone.﴾

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Abd Rabbih narrated to us, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Jubayr ibn Amr al-Qurashi narrated to me, Abu Sa'd al-Ansari narrated to me, from Abu Yahya, the freed slave (mawla) of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The lands are Allah's lands, and the servants are Allah's servants; wherever you find good, then settle there."¹

Thus, when the weak among the Muslims in Makkah found it too constricted to remain there, they went out as emigrants to the land of Abyssinia (al-Habasha), so that they could be safe in their religion there. There they found the best of the two abodes: the Negus (al-Najashi), the king of Abyssinia, Ashama, may Allah have mercy on him, who gave them refuge, supported them with his help, and made them secure in his land. Afterwards, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his remaining companions emigrated to the blessed city of Yathrib, Madinah the radiant.²

Then He said: ﴿Every soul shall taste death; then to Us you will be returned.﴾ That is: wherever you are, death will overtake you, so be in obedience to Allah and where Allah has commanded you, for that is better for you, since death is unavoidable and there is no escape from it. Then the return (al-marji' wa'l-ma'ab) is to Allah. Whoever is obedient to Him, He will reward with the best reward and grant him complete recompense. Therefore He said: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds—We will surely settle them in lofty chambers in Paradise, beneath which rivers flow,﴾ that is: We will surely house them in elevated dwellings in Paradise, beneath which rivers flow, of various kinds: of water, wine, honey and milk, which they will direct and channel wherever they wish; ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, that is: remaining in them eternally, never desiring to be moved from them; ﴿how excellent is the reward of the workers﴾: how excellent these chambers are as a reward for the deeds of the believers.

﴿Those who are patient﴾, that is: patient in their religion, who emigrated to Allah, opposed the enemies, separated from family and relatives, seeking the face of Allah, hoping for what is with Him, and trusting in the truth of His promise.

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: My father narrated to me, Safwan al-Mu'adhdhin narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Sallam narrated to us, from his brother Zayd ibn Sallam, from his grandfather Abu Sallam al-Aswad, who said: Abu Ma'atiq al-Ash'ari narrated to me that Abu Malik al-Ash'ari told him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told him: "Indeed in Paradise there are chambers whose exterior can be seen from the interior and whose interior can be seen from the exterior, which Allah has prepared for those who feed the food, speak good words, fast regularly, and establish prayer while people are asleep."³

And His saying: ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾, in all their circumstances, in their religion and their worldly affairs.

Then Allah informed them that provision is not restricted to one place; rather His provision is general for His creation wherever they are and wherever they may be. Indeed, the provisions of the emigrants, wherever they emigrated, became greater, wider and better, for after a little while they became the rulers of the lands in all regions and cities. Therefore He said: ﴿And how many a creature there is that does not carry its provision﴾, that is: it cannot gather and acquire it, and does not store anything for tomorrow; ﴿Allah provides for it and for you﴾, that is: Allah arranges its provision despite its weakness and makes it easy for it, sending to every creature the provision that suits it, even the ant in the depths of the earth, the bird in the air, and the fish in the water. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon Allah; and He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage. All is in a clear register.﴾ [Hud: 6]

They have mentioned that when the raven hatches its young from eggs, they come out white. When their parents see them thus, they shun them for days until the feathers turn black. The chick remains with its mouth open, seeking its parents, and Allah makes available for it small insects like gnats, which come to it, and it feeds on them during those days until its feathers blacken. Both parents keep checking on it at all times. Whenever they see it with white feathers, they shun it, but when they see its feathers have turned black, they turn to it with care and provision. For this reason the poet said:

O Provider of the young raven in its nest,
and Mender of the broken, shattered bone...

As for the words of the Exalted: ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, meaning: He hears the words of His servants and knows their movements and their stillness.

Allah, the Exalted, affirms [[In T: "informing."]] that there is no deity except Him, because the polytheists who worship others besides Him acknowledge that He alone [[In F: "that"]] created the heavens and the earth, subjected the sun and the moon, and subjected the night and the day. They also acknowledge that He is the Creator who provides for His servants, who determines their lifespans and the differences between them, and who varies their provision, so that some are rich and some are poor. He knows what is good for each of them and who deserves wealth and who deserves poverty. Thus He mentioned that He alone [[In T: "the idols"]] is the one who independently creates things and the sole one who manages them. If this is the case, why is anyone else worshipped? Why is anyone else relied upon? Just as He is One in His dominion, He should be One in worship. Allah, the Exalted, often establishes the station of divinity (uluhiyyah) by means of acknowledging the oneness of lordship (tawhid al-rububiyyah). The polytheists used to acknowledge this, as they would say in their talbiyah: "Here I am, O Allah, with no partner for You, except a partner who is Yours; You own him and what he owns."

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 29, verses 64–66:

He, exalted is He, says, informing about the lowliness of this world, its passing away and its ending, and that it has no permanence, and that the utmost of what is in it is amusement and play: ﴿And indeed, the Last Abode – that is the [true] life﴾, meaning the everlasting life, the truth that has no cessation and no end, but rather it endures forever and ever.

* *

As for His saying ﴿if they only knew﴾, meaning: they would have preferred what remains over what perishes.

Then He informed about the polytheists that when they are in distress they call upon Him alone, with no partner for Him, though this would not be their constant state: ﴿So when they board the ship, they invoke Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾, like His saying ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you invoke fade away except Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away﴾ [al-Isra' 67]. And here He said: ﴿Then when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him﴾.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, he fled from it. When he boarded the sea to go to Abyssinia, the ship was tossed about with them, and its people said: "O people, make your supplication sincerely to your Lord, for none delivers here except Him." Ikrimah said: "By Allah, if none delivers in the sea except Him, then none delivers on land either. O Allah, I make a covenant with You: if I come out [safely], I will go and place my hand in the hand of Muhammad, and I will surely find him kind and merciful." And it was so.

* *

As for His saying ﴿so that they may disbelieve in what We have given them, and so that they may enjoy themselves﴾: many scholars of Arabic grammar, tafsir and the principles of jurisprudence call this the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), because they do not intend this; there is no doubt that it is so with respect to them. But with respect to Allah's decree upon them and His making them subject to it, it is the lam of causation (lam al-ta'lil). We have already established this in His saying ﴿that it might be for them an enemy and a grief﴾ [al-Qasas: 8].
